description: Watchtower weekly-step-02b generated 10 tweets that covered the same underlying angles as the 4 blog drafts written in step-02. The step file explicitly states blog post angles are OFF LIMITS for tweets — not just the titles, but the angle itself. All 10 tweets recycled the same consulting headcount, pilot-to-production, Texas grid, and Anthropic stack themes from the same direction as the drafts. Zero genuine differentiation.
correction: Tweets must approach the underlying topics from genuinely different directions than the blog drafts — different framing, different lens, different audience hook. If a blog draft covers 'The Pyramid Is Coming Down,' a tweet cannot make the same pricing-model argument even without naming the draft. The tweet must take a different cut: a stat reframe, a practitioner moment, a question the draft doesn't ask, a contrarian read on a consensus narrative.
systemic_fix: Updated weekly-step-02b-draft-tweets.md to add an explicit OVERLAP CHECK section with worked examples of compliant vs. non-compliant tweet angles. Added a concrete test: 'If this tweet could be a subtitle of the blog draft, it fails.' Also added a pre-generation checklist requiring Knox to write out the covered territory (not just angle titles but the argument each draft makes) before generating any tweet.
